name: Hyaluronic Acid
benefit: Helps attract and retain water at the skin surface for a hydrated appearance.
note: Often works best when followed by a moisturizer that helps reduce water loss.

name: Glycerin
benefit: A common humectant that helps support hydration in cleansers, serums, and moisturizers.
note: Glycerin appears in many basic products and does not need to be purchased as a separate serum.

name: Ceramides
benefit: Helps support the skin barrier and reduce moisture loss.
note: Ceramides are especially common in moisturizers designed for dry or sensitive skin.

name: Squalane
benefit: Provides lightweight emollient support that can help skin feel softer and less dry.
note: A small amount is usually enough when used as an additional moisturizing step.

name: Panthenol
benefit: Supports hydration and can help skin feel more comfortable and conditioned.
note: Panthenol is frequently combined with other barrier-supporting ingredients.

name: Centella Asiatica
benefit: Commonly used in soothing skincare products intended to support stressed-looking skin.
note: Centella products vary widely, so the full formula matters more than the ingredient name alone.

name: Green Tea
benefit: Used as an antioxidant and soothing ingredient in many lightweight skincare products.
note: Green tea is often combined with hydrating and calming ingredients rather than used alone.

name: Vitamin C
benefit: An antioxidant commonly used to support a brighter and more even-looking complexion.
note: Some vitamin C formulas can be irritating, so beginners may prefer lower-strength or gentler derivatives.

name: Niacinamide
benefit: Supports the skin barrier and is commonly used for uneven tone and oil-control routines.
note: Higher percentages are not always better. Many users do well with moderate concentrations.

name: Azelaic Acid
benefit: Often used to support more even-looking skin and reduce the appearance of post-breakout marks.
note: Introduce slowly if your routine already contains other active treatments.

name: Salicylic Acid
benefit: A beta hydroxy acid commonly used to exfoliate inside oily pores and reduce buildup.
note: Using several exfoliating products at once may increase dryness and irritation.

name: Zinc PCA
benefit: Often included in lightweight products formulated for oily or blemish-prone skin.
note: Zinc is often paired with niacinamide or other oil-supporting ingredients.

name: Glycolic Acid
benefit: An alpha hydroxy acid used to exfoliate the surface of the skin and improve the appearance of texture.
note: Begin gradually and avoid stacking several strong exfoliating treatments in the same routine.

name: Lactic Acid
benefit: An alpha hydroxy acid that provides surface exfoliation and may feel gentler than some stronger acids.
note: Lactic acid can still irritate sensitive skin, particularly when introduced too frequently.

name: Retinol
benefit: A vitamin A derivative used to support skin renewal, texture, and the appearance of fine lines.
note: Start slowly, moisturize well, and avoid combining too many irritating treatments at once.

name: Peptides
benefit: Used in many moisturizers and serums designed to support a smoother and conditioned appearance.
note: Peptide formulas are often easy to add because they do not usually require a separate complicated routine.

name: Mineral Sunscreen
benefit: Uses mineral UV filters such as zinc oxide to provide broad-spectrum sun protection.
note: Choose a sunscreen you can apply generously and consistently rather than chasing a theoretically perfect formula.

name: Centella Sunscreen
benefit: Combines daily UV protection with a formula that may include soothing centella-based ingredients.
note: The sunscreen filters provide UV protection. Centella is an additional supportive ingredient rather than a replacement for proper SPF.
